title: `AVG` of integers is a `DOUBLE`, summed in double
verdict: `avg_int_result`: `DOUBLE`; the sum is a double, so 64-bit inputs lose digits
description: `avg` of any integer type returns `DOUBLE`, and its running sum is a `DOUBLE` too: `avg(9007199254740993, 9007199254740993)` is 9007199254740992.0, and `avg` of two `BIGINT` maxima is 9.223372036854776E18 without an overflow. No values give NULL.
reference: `avg` of `i64` returns `i64` in Substrait; the reference follows the declared output type (`avg_int_result`, #209). Spark's double result needs a cast back, which may be off where the sum passes 2⁵³; `sverify.sql.spark` computes the average exactly from a `DECIMAL(38,0)` sum.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.
